import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Ropelength problems

The *ropelength* of a curve $C$ in $\mathbb{R}^3$ is $\operatorname{Len}(C)/\tau(C)$, the
quotient of its length by its *thickness* $\tau(C)$, the radius of the largest embedded normal
tube around $C$. The ropelength of a knot or link type is the minimal ropelength over all
curves of that type.

Following Cantarella, Kusner and Sullivan (after Gonzalez and Maddocks), the thickness of a
set $L \subseteq \mathbb{R}^3$ is the infimum of the circumradius $r(x, y, z)$ over all
triples of distinct points of $L$, where $r(x, y, z) = \infty$ for collinear triples. Every
curve of positive thickness is $C^{1,1}$, so no regularity needs to be imposed on the curves
over which the infimum is taken.

Thickness is measured as a *radius* (the Hopf link has ropelength $8\pi$), as in
Cantarella–Kusner–Sullivan and in the Wikipedia article.

This file states two open problems from the Wikipedia article:

* the ropelength of a nontrivial knot is bounded by a constant multiple of its crossing number;
* the ropelength of the Borromean rings is $58.006$.

*References:*
* [Wikipedia, Ropelength](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ropelength)
* [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
* J. Cantarella, R. B. Kusner, J. M. Sullivan, *On the minimum ropelength of knots and links*,
  Invent. Math. 150 (2002), [arXiv:math/0103224](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0103224)
* J. Cantarella, J. H. G. Fu, R. B. Kusner, J. M. Sullivan, N. C. Wrinkle, *Criticality for the
  Gehring link problem*, Geom. Topol. 10 (2006),
  [arXiv:math/0402212](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0402212)
* Y. Diao, C. Ernst, A. Por, U. Ziegler, *The ropelengths of knots are almost linear in terms of
  their crossing numbers*, J. Knot Theory Ramifications 28 (2019),
  [doi:10.1142/S0218216519500858](https://doi.org/10.1142/S0218216519500858)
* T. Ashton, J. Cantarella, M. Piatek, E. Rawdon, *Knot tightening by constrained gradient
  descent*, Exp. Math. 20 (2011), [arXiv:1002.1723](https://arxiv.org/abs/1002.1723)
-/

/- ### Knots, links and ambient isotopy -/

blocks.code:
def AmbientIsotopic (A B : Set ℝ³) : Prop :=
  ∃ H : unitInterval → (ℝ³ ≃ₜ ℝ³),
    Continuous (fun p : unitInterval × ℝ³ => H p.1 p.2) ∧
      H 0 = Homeomorph.refl ℝ³ ∧ H 1 '' A = B
blocks.docstring:
Two subsets `A`, `B` of `ℝ³` are *ambient isotopic* if there is a continuous family
`H t`, `t ∈ [0, 1]`, of homeomorphisms of `ℝ³` with `H 0 = id` and `H 1 '' A = B`.
Knot and link types are ambient isotopy classes.

justification.closest_existing_considered: ContinuousMap.Homotopy / ContinuousMap.HomotopyEquiv (homotopy, not isotopy through homeomorphisms)
justification.name: RopelengthProblems.AmbientIsotopic
justification.why_needed: Knot and link types are ambient isotopy classes; Mathlib has homotopies (`ContinuousMap.Homotopy`) but no notion of isotopy through homeomorphisms.

blocks.name: AmbientIsotopic
blocks.text:
/-- Two subsets `A`, `B` of `ℝ³` are *ambient isotopic* if there is a continuous family
`H t`, `t ∈ [0, 1]`, of homeomorphisms of `ℝ³` with `H 0 = id` and `H 1 '' A = B`.
Knot and link types are ambient isotopy classes. -/
def AmbientIsotopic (A B : Set ℝ³) : Prop :=
  ∃ H : unitInterval → (ℝ³ ≃ₜ ℝ³),
    Continuous (fun p : unitInterval × ℝ³ => H p.1 p.2) ∧
      H 0 = Homeomorph.refl ℝ³ ∧ H 1 '' A = B

blocks.code:
@[category API, AMS 57]
theorem AmbientIsotopic.refl (A : Set ℝ³) : AmbientIsotopic A A :=
  ⟨fun _ => Homeomorph.refl ℝ³, continuous_snd, rfl, Set.image_id A⟩
blocks.docstring: Ambient isotopy is reflexive: the constant family of identity maps is an ambient isotopy.
blocks.name: AmbientIsotopic.refl
blocks.text:
/-- Ambient isotopy is reflexive: the constant family of identity maps is an ambient isotopy. -/

theorem AmbientIsotopic.refl (A : Set ℝ³) : AmbientIsotopic A A :=
  ⟨fun _ => Homeomorph.refl ℝ³, continuous_snd, rfl, Set.image_id A⟩

def IsKnot (K : Set ℝ³) : Prop :=
  ∃ γ : Circle → ℝ³, IsEmbedding γ ∧ Set.range γ = K
blocks.docstring: A subset of `ℝ³` is a *knot* if it is the image of a topological embedding of the circle.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Topology.IsEmbedding with domain `Circle` (used as the building block)
justification.name: RopelengthProblems.IsKnot
justification.why_needed: A knot as a subset of ℝ³ homeomorphic to the circle; no knot theory in Mathlib.

def unknot : Set ℝ³ :=
  {p | p 0 ^ 2 + p 1 ^ 2 = 1 ∧ p 2 = 0}
blocks.docstring: The round unit circle in the plane `z = 0`, a representative of the unknot.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Metric.sphere (a 2-sphere in ℝ³, not a circle); EuclideanGeometry.Sphere
justification.name: RopelengthProblems.unknot
justification.why_needed: Concrete representative of the trivial knot, needed to exclude it in slot (i).

def borromeanComponent (i : Fin 3) : Set ℝ³ :=
  {x | x (i + 2) = 0 ∧ x i ^ 2 / 4 + x (i + 1) ^ 2 = 1}
blocks.docstring:
The `i`-th component of the standard configuration of the Borromean rings: an ellipse with
semi-axes `2` and `1` in a coordinate plane. Explicitly, the three components are
* `i = 0`: `{z = 0, x² / 4 + y² = 1}` (in the `xy`-plane, major axis along the `x`-axis),
* `i = 1`: `{x = 0, y² / 4 + z² = 1}` (in the `yz`-plane, major axis along the `y`-axis),
* `i = 2`: `{y = 0, z² / 4 + x² = 1}` (in the `zx`-plane, major axis along the `z`-axis).

justification.name: RopelengthProblems.borromeanComponent
justification.why_needed: The three ellipses of the standard Borromean rings configuration.

blocks.name: borromeanComponent
blocks.text:

  {x | x (i + 2) = 0 ∧ x i ^ 2 / 4 + x (i + 1) ^ 2 = 1}

blocks.code: def borromeanRings : Set ℝ³ := ⋃ i, borromeanComponent i
blocks.docstring:
The standard configuration of the **Borromean rings**: three mutually perpendicular ellipses
with semi-axes `2` and `1`, one in each coordinate plane, with their major axes arranged
cyclically so that each ellipse passes through the disc spanned by the next one, see
`RopelengthProblems.borromeanComponent`. This is the ellipse version of the realization of the
Borromean rings by the three golden rectangles of a regular icosahedron.

justification.closest_existing_considered: None in Mathlib or the repo
justification.name: RopelengthProblems.borromeanRings
justification.why_needed: Concrete representative of the Borromean rings link type for slot (ii).

def borromeanRings : Set ℝ³ := ⋃ i, borromeanComponent i

blocks.code:
@[category test, AMS 57]
theorem pairwise_disjoint_borromeanComponent :
    Pairwise fun i j => Disjoint (borromeanComponent i) (borromeanComponent j) := by
  intro i j hij
  rw [Set.disjoint_left]
  rintro x ⟨hi, hi'⟩ ⟨hj, hj'⟩
  fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j <;> simp only [Fin.isValue, Fin.reduceAdd, Fin.zero_eta,
    Fin.mk_one, Fin.reduceFinMk, ne_eq, not_true_eq_false] at hij hi hi' hj hj' <;>
    rw [hi] at hj' <;> rw [hj] at hi' <;> nlinarith
blocks.docstring: The three components of `borromeanRings` are pairwise disjoint, so it is a link.
blocks.name: pairwise_disjoint_borromeanComponent

  fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j <;> simp only [Fin.isValue, Fin.reduceAdd, Fin.zero_eta,

/- ### Thickness and ropelength -/

blocks.code:
noncomputable def thickness (L : Set ℝ³) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  ⨅ (x ∈ L) (y ∈ L) (z ∈ L) (h : AffineIndependent ℝ ![x, y, z]),
    ENNReal.ofReal (Affine.Simplex.circumradius (⟨![x, y, z], h⟩ : Affine.Simplex ℝ ℝ³ 2))
blocks.docstring:
The *thickness* of a set `L ⊆ ℝ³` (Gonzalez–Maddocks, Cantarella–Kusner–Sullivan):
the infimum, over all triples of distinct points `x y z ∈ L`, of the radius of the circle
through `x`, `y`, `z`. Collinear triples have circumradius `∞` and hence do not contribute to
the infimum, so it suffices to range over affinely independent triples.

For a `C^{1,1}` link this is the radius of the largest embedded normal tube around `L`, and a
curve of positive thickness is automatically `C^{1,1}`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Affine.Simplex.circumradius (used as the building block); Metric.infDist
justification.name: RopelengthProblems.thickness
justification.why_needed: The Gonzalez–Maddocks/CKS thickness (inf of circumradii over triples of points); Mathlib has neither thickness, reach nor normal injectivity radius.

blocks.name: thickness
blocks.text:
/-- The *thickness* of a set `L ⊆ ℝ³` (Gonzalez–Maddocks, Cantarella–Kusner–Sullivan):
the infimum, over all triples of distinct points `x y z ∈ L`, of the radius of the circle
through `x`, `y`, `z`. Collinear triples have circumradius `∞` and hence do not contribute to
the infimum, so it suffices to range over affinely independent triples.

For a `C^{1,1}` link this is the radius of the largest embedded normal tube around `L`, and a
curve of positive thickness is automatically `C^{1,1}`. -/
noncomputable def thickness (L : Set ℝ³) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  ⨅ (x ∈ L) (y ∈ L) (z ∈ L) (h : AffineIndependent ℝ ![x, y, z]),
    ENNReal.ofReal (Affine.Simplex.circumradius (⟨![x, y, z], h⟩ : Affine.Simplex ℝ ℝ³ 2))

blocks.code:
noncomputable def ropelength (L : Set ℝ³) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  μH[1] L / thickness L
blocks.docstring:
The *ropelength* of a set `L ⊆ ℝ³`: its length (one-dimensional Hausdorff measure, which
for a link is the total length of its components) divided by its thickness. It is `∞` if `L`
has zero thickness (and positive length).

justification.closest_existing_considered: MeasureTheory.Measure.hausdorffMeasure 1 (used for length); eVariationOn (parametrised length, not set-based)
justification.name: RopelengthProblems.ropelength
justification.why_needed: Length over thickness of a set.

blocks.name: ropelength
blocks.text:
/-- The *ropelength* of a set `L ⊆ ℝ³`: its length (one-dimensional Hausdorff measure, which
for a link is the total length of its components) divided by its thickness. It is `∞` if `L`
has zero thickness (and positive length). -/
noncomputable def ropelength (L : Set ℝ³) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  μH[1] L / thickness L

blocks.code:
noncomputable def minRopelength (L : Set ℝ³) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  ⨅ (L' : Set ℝ³) (_ : AmbientIsotopic L L'), ropelength L'
blocks.docstring:
The ropelength of the knot or link type of `L`: the infimum of the ropelength over all sets
ambient isotopic to `L`. For a tame link type this infimum is attained (Cantarella, Kusner,
Sullivan); for a wild one it is `∞`.

justification.name: RopelengthProblems.minRopelength
justification.why_needed: The ropelength knot/link invariant: infimum over the ambient isotopy class.

blocks.name: minRopelength
blocks.text:
/-- The ropelength of the knot or link type of `L`: the infimum of the ropelength over all sets
ambient isotopic to `L`. For a tame link type this infimum is attained (Cantarella, Kusner,
Sullivan); for a wild one it is `∞`. -/
noncomputable def minRopelength (L : Set ℝ³) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  ⨅ (L' : Set ℝ³) (_ : AmbientIsotopic L L'), ropelength L'

blocks.code:
@[category API, AMS 57]
theorem minRopelength_le {L L' : Set ℝ³} (h : AmbientIsotopic L L') :
    minRopelength L ≤ ropelength L' :=
  iInf₂_le L' h

/- ### Crossing number -/

blocks.code:
def proj (x : ℝ³) : ℝ × ℝ :=
  (x 0, x 1)

justification.closest_existing_considered: Submodule.orthogonalProjection / ContinuousLinearMap.proj (more indirect for coordinate access)
justification.name: RopelengthProblems.proj
justification.why_needed: Projection of ℝ³ onto the xy-plane used to define knot diagrams.

blocks.name: proj

blocks.code:
structure IsSmoothKnotParam (γ : ℝ → ℝ³) : Prop where
  contDiff : ContDiff ℝ ∞ γ
  periodic : Function.Periodic γ 1
  injOn : Set.InjOn γ (Set.Ico 0 1)
  deriv_ne_zero : ∀ t, deriv γ t ≠ 0
blocks.docstring:
`γ : ℝ → ℝ³` is a *smooth knot parametrisation*: a smooth, `1`-periodic, regular curve
which is injective on a period. Its image is a smooth (in particular tame) knot.

justification.closest_existing_considered: ContDiff, Function.Periodic, Set.InjOn (used as building blocks); ContMDiff on `Circle` (harder to extract tangent vectors)
justification.name: RopelengthProblems.IsSmoothKnotParam
justification.why_needed: Smooth regular closed embedded curves ℝ → ℝ³, the representatives used to define crossing number.

blocks.name: IsSmoothKnotParam
blocks.text:
/-- `γ : ℝ → ℝ³` is a *smooth knot parametrisation*: a smooth, `1`-periodic, regular curve
which is injective on a period. Its image is a smooth (in particular tame) knot. -/
structure IsSmoothKnotParam (γ : ℝ → ℝ³) : Prop where
  contDiff : ContDiff ℝ ∞ γ
  periodic : Function.Periodic γ 1
  injOn : Set.InjOn γ (Set.Ico 0 1)
  deriv_ne_zero : ∀ t, deriv γ t ≠ 0

blocks.code:
def crossings (γ : ℝ → ℝ³) : Set (ℝ × ℝ) :=
  {q | 2 ≤ (Set.range γ ∩ proj ⁻¹' {q}).encard}
blocks.docstring:
The *crossings* of the projection of `γ` to the `xy`-plane: the points of the plane with at
least two preimages on the curve.

justification.name: RopelengthProblems.crossings
justification.why_needed: Set of double points of the planar projection of a curve.

blocks.name: crossings

blocks.code:
structure IsRegularProjection (γ : ℝ → ℝ³) : Prop where
  immersion : ∀ t, proj (deriv γ t) ≠ 0
  finite : (crossings γ).Finite
  encard_le_two : ∀ q, (Set.range γ ∩ proj ⁻¹' {q}).encard ≤ 2
  transverse : ∀ s t, γ s ≠ γ t → proj (γ s) = proj (γ t) →
    LinearIndependent ℝ ![proj (deriv γ s), proj (deriv γ t)]
blocks.docstring:
The projection of `γ` to the `xy`-plane is *regular*: the projected curve is an immersion,
it has only finitely many multiple points, every multiple point is a double point (exactly two
preimages on the curve), and at every double point the two strands cross transversally.

justification.name: RopelengthProblems.IsRegularProjection
justification.why_needed: Textbook regular projection (immersion, finitely many transverse double points), needed to define knot diagrams.

blocks.name: IsRegularProjection
blocks.text:
/-- The projection of `γ` to the `xy`-plane is *regular*: the projected curve is an immersion,
it has only finitely many multiple points, every multiple point is a double point (exactly two
preimages on the curve), and at every double point the two strands cross transversally. -/
structure IsRegularProjection (γ : ℝ → ℝ³) : Prop where
  immersion : ∀ t, proj (deriv γ t) ≠ 0
  finite : (crossings γ).Finite
  encard_le_two : ∀ q, (Set.range γ ∩ proj ⁻¹' {q}).encard ≤ 2
  transverse : ∀ s t, γ s ≠ γ t → proj (γ s) = proj (γ t) →
    LinearIndependent ℝ ![proj (deriv γ s), proj (deriv γ t)]

blocks.code:
noncomputable def crossingNumber (K : Set ℝ³) : ℕ∞ :=
  ⨅ (γ : ℝ → ℝ³) (_ : IsSmoothKnotParam γ) (_ : AmbientIsotopic K (Set.range γ))
    (_ : IsRegularProjection γ), (crossings γ).encard
blocks.docstring:
The *crossing number* of the knot type of `K`: the minimal number of crossings in a knot
diagram of `K`, i.e. in a regular projection to the `xy`-plane of a smooth knot ambient isotopic
to `K`. Every direction of projection is covered, since rotations are ambient isotopies. The
value is `⊤` if `K` has no smooth representative (e.g. for a wild knot).

justification.closest_existing_considered: None in Mathlib (Mathlib's Quandle file only mentions knots in prose)
justification.name: RopelengthProblems.crossingNumber
justification.why_needed: Crossing number of a knot type; absent from Mathlib.

blocks.name: crossingNumber
blocks.text:
/-- The *crossing number* of the knot type of `K`: the minimal number of crossings in a knot
diagram of `K`, i.e. in a regular projection to the `xy`-plane of a smooth knot ambient isotopic
to `K`. Every direction of projection is covered, since rotations are ambient isotopies. The
value is `⊤` if `K` has no smooth representative (e.g. for a wild knot). -/
noncomputable def crossingNumber (K : Set ℝ³) : ℕ∞ :=
  ⨅ (γ : ℝ → ℝ³) (_ : IsSmoothKnotParam γ) (_ : AmbientIsotopic K (Set.range γ))
    (_ : IsRegularProjection γ), (crossings γ).encard

blocks.code:
@[category API, AMS 57]
theorem crossingNumber_le {K : Set ℝ³} {γ : ℝ → ℝ³} (hγ : IsSmoothKnotParam γ)
    (hK : AmbientIsotopic K (Set.range γ)) (hp : IsRegularProjection γ) :
    crossingNumber K ≤ (crossings γ).encard :=
  iInf₂_le_of_le γ hγ <| iInf₂_le hK hp
blocks.name: crossingNumber_le
blocks.text:
@[category API, AMS 57]
theorem crossingNumber_le {K : Set ℝ³} {γ : ℝ → ℝ³} (hγ : IsSmoothKnotParam γ)
    (hK : AmbientIsotopic K (Set.range γ)) (hp : IsRegularProjection γ) :
    crossingNumber K ≤ (crossings γ).encard :=

/- ### The problems -/

blocks.code:
@[category research open, AMS 51 57]
theorem ropelength_problems.parts.i :
    ∃ c : ℝ≥0, 0 < c ∧ ∀ K : Set ℝ³, IsKnot K → ¬ AmbientIsotopic K unknot →
      minRopelength K ≤ c * (crossingNumber K : ℝ≥0∞) := by
  sorry
blocks.docstring:
**Linear ropelength bound.** For every knot $K$ the ropelength $L(K)$ satisfies
$L(K) = O(\operatorname{Cr}(K) \log^5 \operatorname{Cr}(K))$ (Diao, Ernst, Por, Ziegler), and
there are knot families with $L(K) = \Theta(\operatorname{Cr}(K))$. No knot family with
super-linear dependence of ropelength on crossing number has been observed, and it is conjectured
that the tight upper bound is linear: there is a constant $c > 0$ such that
$L(K) \le c \cdot \operatorname{Cr}(K)$ for every nontrivial (tame) knot $K$.

The unknot has crossing number $0$ but positive ropelength ($2\pi$), so it must be excluded.
For a wild knot both the crossing number and the ropelength are infinite, so the inequality
holds trivially and the statement is really about tame knots.

blocks.code:
@[category research open, AMS 51 57]
theorem ropelength_problems.parts.ii :
    minRopelength borromeanRings ∈ Set.Icc (ENNReal.ofReal 58.0055) (ENNReal.ofReal 58.0065) := by
  sorry
blocks.docstring:
**Ropelength of the Borromean rings.** The ropelength of the Borromean rings is conjectured to be
$58.006$: Cantarella, Fu, Kusner, Sullivan and Wrinkle constructed a ropelength-critical
configuration from parametrised arcs (three planar "guitar-shaped" components), with ropelength
approximately $58.0060$ in units where the thickness is the radius of the tube, and it is
conjectured to be the minimiser. Since $58.006$ is a rounded figure, the statement asserts that
the minimum ropelength agrees with $58.006$ to three decimal places, i.e. lies in
$[58.0055, 58.0065]$.

end RopelengthProblems

context:
In physical knot theory, each realization of a link or knot has an associated ropelength. Intuitively this is the minimal length of an ideally flexible rope that is needed to tie a given link, or knot. Knots and links that minimize ropelength are called ideal knots and ideal links respectively.
The ropelength problem is open: neither for knots nor for open knots in a long rope has an expression been found (in 2026) that describes the ropelength of tight, ideal knots. The problem is unsolved (as of 2026) for every non-trivial knot.

For slot (ii) I chose the rounding-tolerance reading [58.0055, 58.0065] (agreement with 58.006 to three decimal places) rather than the truncation interval [58.006, 58.007) suggested as an example in the notes, since the CFKSW value is only known to be ≈ 58.0060 and a rounding tolerance is the standard reading of a rounded figure.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Ropelength problems

The *ropelength* of a curve $C$ in $\mathbb{R}^3$ is $\operatorname{Len}(C)/\tau(C)$, the
quotient of its length by its *thickness* $\tau(C)$, the radius of the largest embedded normal
tube around $C$. The ropelength of a knot or link type is the minimal ropelength over all
curves of that type.

Following Cantarella, Kusner and Sullivan (after Gonzalez and Maddocks), the thickness of a
set $L \subseteq \mathbb{R}^3$ is the infimum of the circumradius $r(x, y, z)$ over all
triples of distinct points of $L$, where $r(x, y, z) = \infty$ for collinear triples. Every
curve of positive thickness is $C^{1,1}$, so no regularity needs to be imposed on the curves
over which the infimum is taken.

Thickness is measured as a *radius* (the Hopf link has ropelength $8\pi$), as in
Cantarella–Kusner–Sullivan and in the Wikipedia article.

This file states two open problems from the Wikipedia article:

* the ropelength of a nontrivial knot is bounded by a constant multiple of its crossing number;
* the ropelength of the Borromean rings is $58.006$.

*References:*
* [Wikipedia, Ropelength](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ropelength)
* [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
* J. Cantarella, R. B. Kusner, J. M. Sullivan, *On the minimum ropelength of knots and links*,
  Invent. Math. 150 (2002), [arXiv:math/0103224](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0103224)
* J. Cantarella, J. H. G. Fu, R. B. Kusner, J. M. Sullivan, N. C. Wrinkle, *Criticality for the
  Gehring link problem*, Geom. Topol. 10 (2006),
  [arXiv:math/0402212](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0402212)
* Y. Diao, C. Ernst, A. Por, U. Ziegler, *The ropelengths of knots are almost linear in terms of
  their crossing numbers*, J. Knot Theory Ramifications 28 (2019),
  [doi:10.1142/S0218216519500858](https://doi.org/10.1142/S0218216519500858)
* T. Ashton, J. Cantarella, M. Piatek, E. Rawdon, *Knot tightening by constrained gradient
  descent*, Exp. Math. 20 (2011), [arXiv:1002.1723](https://arxiv.org/abs/1002.1723)
-/

open MeasureTheory Topology
open scoped EuclideanGeometry ContDiff ENNReal NNReal

namespace RopelengthProblems

/- ### Knots, links and ambient isotopy -/

/-- Two subsets `A`, `B` of `ℝ³` are *ambient isotopic* if there is a continuous family
`H t`, `t ∈ [0, 1]`, of homeomorphisms of `ℝ³` with `H 0 = id` and `H 1 '' A = B`.
Knot and link types are ambient isotopy classes. -/
def AmbientIsotopic (A B : Set ℝ³) : Prop :=
  ∃ H : unitInterval → (ℝ³ ≃ₜ ℝ³),
    Continuous (fun p : unitInterval × ℝ³ => H p.1 p.2) ∧
      H 0 = Homeomorph.refl ℝ³ ∧ H 1 '' A = B

/-- Ambient isotopy is reflexive: the constant family of identity maps is an ambient isotopy. -/
@[category API, AMS 57]
theorem AmbientIsotopic.refl (A : Set ℝ³) : AmbientIsotopic A A :=
  ⟨fun _ => Homeomorph.refl ℝ³, continuous_snd, rfl, Set.image_id A⟩

/-- A subset of `ℝ³` is a *knot* if it is the image of a topological embedding of the circle. -/
def IsKnot (K : Set ℝ³) : Prop :=
  ∃ γ : Circle → ℝ³, IsEmbedding γ ∧ Set.range γ = K

/-- The round unit circle in the plane `z = 0`, a representative of the unknot. -/
def unknot : Set ℝ³ :=
  {p | p 0 ^ 2 + p 1 ^ 2 = 1 ∧ p 2 = 0}

/-- The `i`-th component of the standard configuration of the Borromean rings: an ellipse with
semi-axes `2` and `1` in a coordinate plane. Explicitly, the three components are
* `i = 0`: `{z = 0, x² / 4 + y² = 1}` (in the `xy`-plane, major axis along the `x`-axis),
* `i = 1`: `{x = 0, y² / 4 + z² = 1}` (in the `yz`-plane, major axis along the `y`-axis),
* `i = 2`: `{y = 0, z² / 4 + x² = 1}` (in the `zx`-plane, major axis along the `z`-axis). -/
def borromeanComponent (i : Fin 3) : Set ℝ³ :=
  {x | x (i + 2) = 0 ∧ x i ^ 2 / 4 + x (i + 1) ^ 2 = 1}

/-- The standard configuration of the **Borromean rings**: three mutually perpendicular ellipses
with semi-axes `2` and `1`, one in each coordinate plane, with their major axes arranged
cyclically so that each ellipse passes through the disc spanned by the next one, see
`RopelengthProblems.borromeanComponent`. This is the ellipse version of the realization of the
Borromean rings by the three golden rectangles of a regular icosahedron. -/
def borromeanRings : Set ℝ³ := ⋃ i, borromeanComponent i

/-- The three components of `borromeanRings` are pairwise disjoint, so it is a link. -/
@[category test, AMS 57]
theorem pairwise_disjoint_borromeanComponent :
    Pairwise fun i j => Disjoint (borromeanComponent i) (borromeanComponent j) := by
  intro i j hij
  rw [Set.disjoint_left]
  rintro x ⟨hi, hi'⟩ ⟨hj, hj'⟩
  fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j <;> simp only [Fin.isValue, Fin.reduceAdd, Fin.zero_eta,
    Fin.mk_one, Fin.reduceFinMk, ne_eq, not_true_eq_false] at hij hi hi' hj hj' <;>
    rw [hi] at hj' <;> rw [hj] at hi' <;> nlinarith

/- ### Thickness and ropelength -/

/-- The *thickness* of a set `L ⊆ ℝ³` (Gonzalez–Maddocks, Cantarella–Kusner–Sullivan):
the infimum, over all triples of distinct points `x y z ∈ L`, of the radius of the circle
through `x`, `y`, `z`. Collinear triples have circumradius `∞` and hence do not contribute to
the infimum, so it suffices to range over affinely independent triples.

For a `C^{1,1}` link this is the radius of the largest embedded normal tube around `L`, and a
curve of positive thickness is automatically `C^{1,1}`. -/
noncomputable def thickness (L : Set ℝ³) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  ⨅ (x ∈ L) (y ∈ L) (z ∈ L) (h : AffineIndependent ℝ ![x, y, z]),
    ENNReal.ofReal (Affine.Simplex.circumradius (⟨![x, y, z], h⟩ : Affine.Simplex ℝ ℝ³ 2))

/-- The *ropelength* of a set `L ⊆ ℝ³`: its length (one-dimensional Hausdorff measure, which
for a link is the total length of its components) divided by its thickness. It is `∞` if `L`
has zero thickness (and positive length). -/
noncomputable def ropelength (L : Set ℝ³) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  μH[1] L / thickness L

/-- The ropelength of the knot or link type of `L`: the infimum of the ropelength over all sets
ambient isotopic to `L`. For a tame link type this infimum is attained (Cantarella, Kusner,
Sullivan); for a wild one it is `∞`. -/
noncomputable def minRopelength (L : Set ℝ³) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  ⨅ (L' : Set ℝ³) (_ : AmbientIsotopic L L'), ropelength L'

@[category API, AMS 57]
theorem minRopelength_le {L L' : Set ℝ³} (h : AmbientIsotopic L L') :
    minRopelength L ≤ ropelength L' :=
  iInf₂_le L' h

/- ### Crossing number -/

/-- Orthogonal projection of `ℝ³` onto the `xy`-plane. -/
def proj (x : ℝ³) : ℝ × ℝ :=
  (x 0, x 1)

/-- `γ : ℝ → ℝ³` is a *smooth knot parametrisation*: a smooth, `1`-periodic, regular curve
which is injective on a period. Its image is a smooth (in particular tame) knot. -/
structure IsSmoothKnotParam (γ : ℝ → ℝ³) : Prop where
  contDiff : ContDiff ℝ ∞ γ
  periodic : Function.Periodic γ 1
  injOn : Set.InjOn γ (Set.Ico 0 1)
  deriv_ne_zero : ∀ t, deriv γ t ≠ 0

/-- The *crossings* of the projection of `γ` to the `xy`-plane: the points of the plane with at
least two preimages on the curve. -/
def crossings (γ : ℝ → ℝ³) : Set (ℝ × ℝ) :=
  {q | 2 ≤ (Set.range γ ∩ proj ⁻¹' {q}).encard}

/-- The projection of `γ` to the `xy`-plane is *regular*: the projected curve is an immersion,
it has only finitely many multiple points, every multiple point is a double point (exactly two
preimages on the curve), and at every double point the two strands cross transversally. -/
structure IsRegularProjection (γ : ℝ → ℝ³) : Prop where
  immersion : ∀ t, proj (deriv γ t) ≠ 0
  finite : (crossings γ).Finite
  encard_le_two : ∀ q, (Set.range γ ∩ proj ⁻¹' {q}).encard ≤ 2
  transverse : ∀ s t, γ s ≠ γ t → proj (γ s) = proj (γ t) →
    LinearIndependent ℝ ![proj (deriv γ s), proj (deriv γ t)]

/-- The *crossing number* of the knot type of `K`: the minimal number of crossings in a knot
diagram of `K`, i.e. in a regular projection to the `xy`-plane of a smooth knot ambient isotopic
to `K`. Every direction of projection is covered, since rotations are ambient isotopies. The
value is `⊤` if `K` has no smooth representative (e.g. for a wild knot). -/
noncomputable def crossingNumber (K : Set ℝ³) : ℕ∞ :=
  ⨅ (γ : ℝ → ℝ³) (_ : IsSmoothKnotParam γ) (_ : AmbientIsotopic K (Set.range γ))
    (_ : IsRegularProjection γ), (crossings γ).encard

@[category API, AMS 57]
theorem crossingNumber_le {K : Set ℝ³} {γ : ℝ → ℝ³} (hγ : IsSmoothKnotParam γ)
    (hK : AmbientIsotopic K (Set.range γ)) (hp : IsRegularProjection γ) :
    crossingNumber K ≤ (crossings γ).encard :=
  iInf₂_le_of_le γ hγ <| iInf₂_le hK hp

/- ### The problems -/

/--
**Linear ropelength bound.** For every knot $K$ the ropelength $L(K)$ satisfies
$L(K) = O(\operatorname{Cr}(K) \log^5 \operatorname{Cr}(K))$ (Diao, Ernst, Por, Ziegler), and
there are knot families with $L(K) = \Theta(\operatorname{Cr}(K))$. No knot family with
super-linear dependence of ropelength on crossing number has been observed, and it is conjectured
that the tight upper bound is linear: there is a constant $c > 0$ such that
$L(K) \le c \cdot \operatorname{Cr}(K)$ for every nontrivial (tame) knot $K$.

The unknot has crossing number $0$ but positive ropelength ($2\pi$), so it must be excluded.
For a wild knot both the crossing number and the ropelength are infinite, so the inequality
holds trivially and the statement is really about tame knots.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 51 57]
theorem ropelength_problems.parts.i :
    ∃ c : ℝ≥0, 0 < c ∧ ∀ K : Set ℝ³, IsKnot K → ¬ AmbientIsotopic K unknot →
      minRopelength K ≤ c * (crossingNumber K : ℝ≥0∞) := by
  sorry

/--
**Ropelength of the Borromean rings.** The ropelength of the Borromean rings is conjectured to be
$58.006$: Cantarella, Fu, Kusner, Sullivan and Wrinkle constructed a ropelength-critical
configuration from parametrised arcs (three planar "guitar-shaped" components), with ropelength
approximately $58.0060$ in units where the thickness is the radius of the tube, and it is
conjectured to be the minimiser. Since $58.006$ is a rounded figure, the statement asserts that
the minimum ropelength agrees with $58.006$ to three decimal places, i.e. lies in
$[58.0055, 58.0065]$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 51 57]
theorem ropelength_problems.parts.ii :
    minRopelength borromeanRings ∈ Set.Icc (ENNReal.ofReal 58.0055) (ENNReal.ofReal 58.0065) := by
  sorry

end RopelengthProblems

items: Knots and links are modelled as subsets of ℝ³ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3) (following CKS, who work with curves as sets); a knot is the image of a topological embedding of `Circle`. Knot/link types are ambient isotopy classes: `AmbientIsotopic A B` is a continuous family `H : unitInterval → (ℝ³ ≃ₜ ℝ³)` (jointly continuous forward map) with `H 0 = id` and `H 1 '' A = B`.

Thickness follows Cantarella–Kusner–Sullivan / Gonzalez–Maddocks: the infimum over triples of distinct points of the circumradius, with collinear triples contributing ∞. Since collinear triples never lower the infimum, the Lean definition ranges over affinely independent triples and uses Mathlib's `Affine.Simplex.circumradius`. Thickness is the tube RADIUS (Hopf link has ropelength 8π), matching the article's convention and the 58.006 figure.

Length is the 1-dimensional Hausdorff measure μH[1] (equals arc length for rectifiable Jordan curves; Mathlib's normalization gives μH[1] = volume on ℝ). Ropelength of a set is μH[1] L / thickness L in ℝ≥0∞, which is ⊤ when thickness is 0; hence the infimum over the isotopy class (`minRopelength`) needs no explicit C^{1,1} restriction: CKS show positive thickness forces C^{1,1}, and wild types get ropelength ⊤.

Crossing number is defined via smooth representatives: `IsSmoothKnotParam γ` is a C^∞, 1-periodic, regular curve ℝ → ℝ³ injective on a period; the projection direction is fixed to the z-axis (`proj x = (x 0, x 1)`), which loses no generality since rotations are ambient isotopies; `IsRegularProjection` is the textbook notion (immersed projection, finitely many multiple points, each a double point with exactly two preimages, transverse strands); `crossingNumber K : ℕ∞` is the infimum of the number of double points, so it is ⊤ for wild knots (no smooth representative). Consequently slot (i) is trivially true for wild knots (RHS = c·⊤ = ⊤), which is why `0 < c` is included; this implements the notes' restriction to tame knots without a separate tameness predicate.

‘Nontrivial knot’ is formalised as not ambient isotopic to the round unit circle `unknot = {p | p 0 ^ 2 + p 1 ^ 2 = 1 ∧ p 2 = 0}`; the unknot has Cr = 0 but ropelength 2π so it must be excluded, as in the decomposition notes.

The constant is `c : ℝ≥0` with `0 < c`, multiplied in ℝ≥0∞ against the ℕ∞ → ℝ≥0∞ coercion of the crossing number. This is the O(Cr(K)) statement; additive constants are not allowed (unnecessary once the unknot is excluded, since Cr ≥ 3 for nontrivial knots).

The Borromean rings are the standard configuration of three mutually perpendicular ellipses with semi-axes 2 and 1, arranged cyclically (x²/4 + y² = 1 in z = 0; y²/4 + z² = 1 in x = 0; z²/4 + x² = 1 in y = 0); this is the mirror image of the golden-rectangle realisation from the icosahedron, and the Borromean rings are amphichiral. A reviewer should confirm the cyclic arrangement (the components are pairwise disjoint; the non-cyclic arrangement with equal axes would intersect).

The value 58.006 in the statement is a rounded figure (CFKSW's configuration has length ≈ 58.0060; Ridgerunner's numerical upper bound is 58.0070), so slot (ii) is stated as the ropelength lying in the closed interval [58.0055, 58.0065], i.e. agreeing with 58.006 to three decimal places. The endpoint convention (closed vs. half-open) is immaterial. The ordinary (CKS) ropelength is used, as in the Wikipedia article, not the Gehring ropelength for which CFKSW proved criticality.
Ropelength of a link is total length (μH[1] of the union) over the thickness of the whole set (triples may involve different components), exactly as in CKS.

Compiles with only 'declaration uses sorry' warnings. Ambiguities: (1) 58.006 is a rounded figure; I used the rounding interval [58.0055, 58.0065] (closed) rather than [58.006, 58.007) — both contain the CFKSW value 58.0060 but the rounding reading is the standard interpretation of a rounded decimal. (2) The linear-bound conjecture is stated for tame knots via the ℕ∞-valued crossing number (⊤ for wild knots makes the bound vacuous for them), with the unknot excluded as a hypothesis rather than via an additive constant. (3) Knot/link types are unoriented ambient isotopy classes of subsets of ℝ³; mirror images are not identified, which is immaterial since ropelength is reflection-invariant and the Borromean rings are amphichiral. Dropped items in the decomposition are correctly dropped. c07 should not be used: its crossing number is provably wrong (vertex–vertex coincidences uncounted), making slot (i) false. c08 (full bail-out) reasons are unconvincing given that the needed notions (thickness via circumradius, Hausdorff length, ambient isotopy, regular projections) are definable with existing Mathlib primitives.
